title: UPSERT: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT
description: Implement race-condition-free upserts with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE and DO NOTHING targeting unique constraints or partial indexes.

data.text: In concurrent applications, doing a `SELECT` check before an `INSERT` leads to race conditions (two transactions check simultaneously, see no record, and both attempt to insert, causing unique constraint violations). PostgreSQL solves this with native **UPSERT**: `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT`.
ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE vs DO NOTHING

data.title: Atomic Counter Upsert with EXCLUDED Pseudo-Table
data.content: Increments page view count or inserts initial view record atomically.
data.code:
INSERT INTO page_views (page_url, view_count, last_visited_at)
VALUES ('/courses/postgresql', 1, NOW())
ON CONFLICT (page_url) 
DO UPDATE SET 
    view_count = page_views.view_count + 1,
    last_visited_at = EXCLUDED.last_visited_at
RETURNING page_url, view_count;

data.title: The `EXCLUDED` Pseudo-Table
data.text: `EXCLUDED` represents the row that was proposed for insertion. Referencing `EXCLUDED.col` lets you apply the incoming value to the existing row.
Bulk Upserts and Partial Unique Indexes

data.title: Upsert a whole staging table
data.content: The conflict target must match a unique constraint or unique index. In the same statement you can update every existing row from the incoming set.
data.code:
INSERT INTO products (sku, price, updated_at)
SELECT sku, price, now()
FROM staging_products
ON CONFLICT (sku) DO UPDATE
SET price      = EXCLUDED.price,
    updated_at = EXCLUDED.updated_at;

data.title: Conflicting only against active rows
data.content: A partial unique index lets soft-deleted rows share the same email while blocking duplicates among active users. ON CONFLICT must repeat the index predicate to infer it.
data.code:
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_users_active_email
ON users (email)
WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

INSERT INTO users (email, name)
VALUES ('ada@example.com', 'Ada')
ON CONFLICT (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL DO NOTHING
RETURNING id, email;

data.title: Interview angle: upsert concurrency
data.text: ON CONFLICT is the correct atomic upsert, but it is not a silver bullet. It only handles unique conflicts, so a row that disappears between the read and the write still errors. Under `SERIALIZABLE` isolation, concurrent upserts can raise serialization failures that the application must retry. Being able to compare ON CONFLICT with MERGE and with a retry loop is a strong interview answer.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `ON CONFLICT` provides atomic, race-condition-free upsert behavior.
Target column must have an active `UNIQUE` constraint or unique index.
Use `EXCLUDED.column_name` to reference incoming values in the update statement.
